recipes.name: Homestyle Kalua Pork with Cabbage in a Slow Cooker

steps.text: Combine salt, pepper, and ground ginger in a bowl; evenly rub onto pork roast then place into a slow cooker.
Whisk soy sauce, Worcestershire sauce, and liquid smoke together in a bowl; pour over pork roast. Cover slow cooker.
Cook on Low for 10 hours. Add cabbage to slow cooker; cook 30 minutes more. Shred pork to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Homestyle Kalua Pork with Cabbage in a Slow Cooker
raw_recipe.description: Simmer a pork shoulder roast in a slow cooker for 10 hours with a ginger-spiked sauce for tender and tasty shredded Hawaiian-style pork.

review.reviewBody: Having been to a couple of luaus now, this effectively recreates the taste as well as you can without burying a pig in your back yard. We used a low sodium soy sauce, which was fine as their is more than enough salt in the recipe. We cooked a 4 lb butt in the slow cooker for about 8 hours, steaming with the cabbage for the last 30 minutes. The result was great. I served it with Guam styled fried rice, so it was a real gut buster feast. While buns or rolls are somewhat traditional, as a low glutein household we don't feel they are required. in fact, the first time I served this with hot dog buns the bread was ignored entirely, as everyone was perfectly full with pork, cabbage, rice and vegetables. while not anyone's idea of a health nut dinner, this is certainly a good option if you want a breadless meal.

Excellent Kalua Pork. Thanks for the recipe Mei. I chose this recipe over others because it called for ginger, worcestershire, and some soy sauce vs. just salt and liquid smoke, which I feel flavored the roast much better.

 I also used medium grain Hawaiian Alaea Sea Salt. If you do use a granule salt, like I did, whether it be Kosher or Hawaiian, assure that you first crush it with a mortar and pestle, and cut the salt back if you don't like your meat very salty. 

I also served the pork over a bed of the steamed cabbage leaves just as it was served to us at "Feast at Lele" Luau in Maui last month. I would recommend this for two reasons. First, this is a lot of pork and since there were lots of left over’s, I wanted my cabbage steamed fresh when eating it again, not soggy as it would be when you reheat it with the cabbage mixed in. Second, I also added Mexican spices,(Chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, onion powder, cayenne pepper. etc..), and made some delicious shredded
pork tacos for lunch one day.

I will be making this recipe again many times in the future.

My family loved it. I used all the ingredients as called out(except cabbage) but I made it in my Instantpot instead of the crock pot. Because I cooked it this way, I actually cut up the meat in bigger chunks maybe 2-3", I put those in a bowl and and tossed the dry mixture on the meat to evenly cover, then I poured the wet mixture and tried to evenly cover as well. I added 3/4 of a cup of water to the base of the instantpot, put the meat in, covered, set it for 40 minutes and did a natural release of 15 minutes at the end. Then shredded and served. All of my family loved it and thought it tasted just like what we order from our favorite Hawaiian restaurant.

I made this in the last couple weeks 3 times my boyfriend loves loves it. This is his favorite meal now. I used the low sodium soy sauce, about a tablespoon of Worcestershire sauce since we love it so much, a couple tablespoons of minced garlic and a cup of low sodium chicken broth. I throw it in my instant pot for about a hour and 45 minutes high pressure. Once it finished I throw the cabbage on high pressure for 2 minutes. Absolutely amazing our favorite recipe.

Kudos!!! I have to admit...half-way through the cooking process, I said to myself, "Hey, I know where this is going!" So, I added 1/4 cup packed brown sugar, 1/2 cup of my homemade golden plum sweet BBQ sauce, and 4 tablespoons of Yashidas sauce. Then, I replaced the top...and waited...and waited. To make a long story short, the cabbage tasted like it had been bathed in butter, and you'll all have a hard time keeping pieces in a fork. I served it with a blend of Brown and Basmati White Rice, with chopped sweet onion, using vegetable broth, 1 teaspoon each of Better-than-Bouillion chicken and beef (doing this makes the greatest pork flavor goin') as the moisture (not water!) OMG!!! 
The following day, I added 1 tablespoon each of McCormick Smokehouse Maple, and Vanns Spices Harissa. Heated it back up in a smaller crockpot, added sauteed sweet vidalia onions with brown sugar to caramelize'em, then served this onto Onion Hamburger Buns, with shredded Mexican blend cheese, with a spread of mayonaisse/honey mustard/sweet basil/worchestershire sauce, and lettuce.
After the tears and the folks could talk coherently once again, they just stared at me and asked, What was that?" I told'em what it was and where to find it. Get ready gang. Keep yer spats straight.
Jim Lyman, Master Chef (ret)

One of the best pork slowcooker dishes I've ever made, and waaay better than anything I've eaten outside of Hawaii.

Cut the kosher salt down to about one heaping tablespoon, and use another big tablespoon of soy + a dash. Good liquid smoke is important, get some hickory flavored (I'm not a huge mesquite fan).

What really set if off for me was that I rubbed the pork in brown sugar, about 2 tablespoons, before pouring on the sauce. I think this gave a great balance.

Added the cabbage after I got home and put on low for another hour, it was perfect. Also, my roast was only 2.5 lbs., so for a 5 pounder, the sodium is probably about right. Ignore the whiners, this one just works.

This recipe was soooo good! My whole family absolutely loved it!!! I made the pork shoulder in the crock pot as directed. I had my son get the cabbage and he came home with a 4-lb head of cabbage! I quick steamed the cabbage in about two inches of chicken broth in a separate pan, right before serving. I sliced the cabbage up by cutting it first in have and then slicing it in 1 inch pieces and I put those in the pot of steaming chicken broth. It took just 5-7 minutes before it was crisp cooked and ready to serve. I didn't add any extra salt in the cabbage as the review said it was "salty". I also quick cooked some red potatoes cut up and some fresh green beans as another side for this. Again, no salt added just in case the meat was really salty. We lifted the pork out of the crock pot and pulled it in a baking dish. Then we poured the juices into a measuring cup so we could sparingly add it to our dish, as needed. Wow!! what a hit. And even though it was a slow cooker dinner (usually reserved for winter meals) it was a nice and refreshing meal even for 90 degree weather. Will definitely make again. It was so delicious we even enjoyed it as a leftover meal..

I very much enjoyed this dish. I cut down on the salt by half and added a bit more of the liquid smoke. Once the roast was done cooking I put the cabbage in put I noticed it took more than 30 mins for the cabbage to soften so I let it cook longer. In the meantime I did a taste test and decided to add some water to help with the cabbage and in addition I also added some crushed pineapples to the mixture as well. I knew that it would give the dish a sweet taste to balance out the smokiness(which I was totally correct). After everything was done I put it on hot dog bun and squeezed some bbq sauce on it and I can say that it was amazing... It tasted wonderful before I added the enhancements but i believe I made it better... Also the water does make it soupy so don't add too much but I believe it is necessary to help the cabbage soften.

I followed the recipe except: I first seared the pork, cut it in third and used fresh ginger. I guess I should have cut it up then seared it but that's not how it happened. It turned out wonderful and my husband ate too much. I will definitely make this again. Thanks so much!

I created this in my Instant Pot (pressure cooker) and wanted to update for those who might want it in less than an hour. I used a 1 1/4 lb boneless pork loin, half a head of chopped cabbage and added an 8 ox potato with the skin on and diced large. Trimmed the pork and followed the recipe. I used hickory smoke flavor. Set my IP on meat for 55 min and used quick release since we were hungry. I had a friend over and she had 3 servings. My husband raved about it. No leftovers! I'd keep everything the same but would add as much cabbage as my pot would hold. It really shrunk down in the cooking.

I will own that I decided to double all the ingredients except the pork to give this a more prominent flavor. Unfortunately, I found this much too smoky and couldn’t taste anything else. I also didn’t think the cabbage added anything. And, I think I was missing a properly prepared side dish like rice or a vegetable. Instead - I served this like a twist off of pulled pork and served on sweet Hawaiian buns. Was the meat tender? Yes. I just found okay good. Thanks for sharing Mei!
Excellent recipe..we think we are in Hawaii!
I love pork and my slow cooker! This is such a tasty recipe! I usually put this together with Kim's macaroni salad from here, and some pineapple. Much cheaper than a trip to Hawai'i! But sooooo good!
The whole family absolutely loved this! I didn't change a thing to the recipe, it's perfect as it is. I served it with rice and chopped pineapple on the side. Fabulous!
This recipe has become a family favorite. It is so good and a good way to feed a crowd
Nice and easy and very delicious. We paired it with the coconut lime rice.

I made this without the cabbage and added an extra TBL of soy sauce. 10hrs on low and it turned out fantastic. Stored the leftovers in the juices and leftovers were even better. This will be a recipe that I will use a lot in the future.
